title: Spike (round 2): pi-durable as ticfac's single worker harness, local and cloud — harness beside the orchestrator, tools in the container, storage that outlives it
description: Round 1 (#207, docs/spikes/n0b-pi-durable-harness.md) tested Cloudflare's PiHarness-in-a-DO packaging: agent loop survives eviction/redeploy, but a dead container loses clone/edits/cache; verdict 'later'. Round 2 looks at Earendil's own Pi Durable (https://earendil.com/posts/pi-durable/, repo github.com/earendil-works/pi packages/durable, MIT, experimental): runtime-agnostic (memory/SQLite/JSONL storage, no Node-only APIs), every model call and tool call a checkpointed task, a NEW process resumes from the same storage, storage separated from execution ('harness on one machine, tools on another' via execution-environment adapters), one harness runs many conversations, any number of clients can attach to watch/steer. Question: should pi-durable be ticfac's ONE worker harness everywhere — the harness hosted beside the orchestrator (local process / orchestrator container / a DO), tools executed in the worker container (FactorySandbox, umq) or a local worktree via an execution adapter — giving (a) crash resume across processes, (b) the same harness local and cloud, (c) live watch/steer of worker conversations in ticfac watch (thinking, tool calls; f6o heartbeat) and stuck nudges as real steering. Operator, 2026-10-04: consider storage in different Cloudflare stores — e.g. D1 (SQL), JSONL in R2, DO SQLite (+ K2 streams for the live event fan-out) — compare durability, latency per checkpoint, cost, size limits, multi-reader watch. Pair with the workspace half: wip commits as the worker goes and/or container snapshots, so a resumed turn has its files. Prototype: kill the harness process mid-tool and the container mid-turn; show resume with workspace restored; one storage backend in a CF store. Deliver a decision doc + epic sketch.
notes:
2026-10-04 12:16 - Spike done: docs/spikes/n0b-pi-durable-harness.md (PR #207). Feasible (staging prototype: DO eviction/redeploy mid-tool resumes; 17-min tool call ok) but recommended LATER: container death still loses the workspace, umq removes the rollout cause, packages experimental. Cheaper alternative: persist+resume pi CLI session in a fresh container.
2026-10-04 13:33 - Round 2 done: docs/spikes/n0b-round2-pi-durable.md (PR #210, a45306b). Recommend ADOPT pi-durable as the single worker harness behind a harness=pi-durable flag: cloud = WorkerAgent DO per attempt on its own DO SQLite + FactorySandbox ExecutionEnv; local = Node harness per worker on local SQLite + worktree env; wip commit per tool round. Prototype: harness kill -9 mid-tool -> new process reattached to the same container process; container destroyed mid-command -> workspace restored from wip checkpoint (~26 s) and the turn finished; second client watched + steered live across a harness restart. Storage: DO SQLite ~9 ms/commit (+20 ms hop), D1 ~12 ms but needs a new Storage impl, R2 186 ms no append, local SQLite 0.1 ms, K2 unmeasured (no k2 scopes). 9-step epic sketch in the doc.
acceptance_criteria: [1] Decision doc committed: architecture, storage comparison (D1 / R2 JSONL / DO SQLite / local), what it fixes, risks (experimental API), recommendation. [2] Prototype evidence of cross-process resume with workspace restored. [3] If adopt: an epic sketch with PR-sized steps.
closed_reason: Spike round 2 done: docs/spikes/n0b-round2-pi-durable.md (PR #210) — adopt behind a flag; epic sketch in the doc
